title: Topic 01, Part 01 - The Purpose of a Database

best.what: why a database is more than a bucket: organization + querying
real-world hierarchical relationships (dept has many employees, etc.)

why: Clean, jargon-light intro to why databases exist at all; no SQL. Perfect opener for the kids' database unit.

title: Topic 01, Part 02 - Problems with Storing Data in a List

best.what: redundancy when storing repeat customer/order info in one list
storing multiple themes (customer+product+salesperson) in one row

why: Makes the exact case for why a single flat Sheet tab breaks down, using relatable retail examples.

title: Topic 01, Part 03 - List Modification Issues

best.what: insert/delete/update anomalies walked through with a car-repair-shop list example

why: The clearest, most concrete explanation in the whole course of insert/update/delete anomalies; directly motivates splitting a Sheet into tabs.

title: Topic 01, Part 04 - Introduction to Relational Databases

best.what: one table per business concept + joining tables back together
matched pairs of values (IDs) linking rows across tables, drawn live

why: This is the single best video for teaching 'one tab per concept, linked by an ID column' -- exactly how the kids' Google Sheet database should be structured.

title: Topic 01, Part 05 - The Purpose and Value of the Structured Query Language (SQL)

best.what: the idea of 'asking the database questions' in plain English

why: Good framing of querying-as-asking-questions, but its selling point (SQL is a universal standard) doesn't matter to kids who never write SQL -- Gemini does. Useful context for the guide writer only.

title: Topic 01, Part 06 - An Overview of Database Systems

best.what: users -> app -> DBMS -> database chain, and why only the DBMS touches the data (security gatekeeper)

why: Explains the user/app/database-layer chain that maps directly onto their Gemini-app-plus-Sheets-backend architecture, including why you never let the front end touch the data directly.

title: Topic 01, Part 07 - Users and Databases - Components of a Database System

best.what: ER diagrams, many-to-many relationships, and the lookup/associative table pattern (customers x courses x enrollment)

why: The many-to-many / lookup-table explanation (drawn live with a customer-course-enrollment example) is exactly the pattern kids will need for things like players x items x inventory in a Sheet.

title: Topic 01, Part 08 - The DBMS and Database Applications - Components of a Database System

best.what: range constraints and referential integrity, explained with a year-of-birth example and a live 'invalid row' demo

why: Constraints and referential integrity map directly onto data-validation rules and 'does this ID actually exist' bugs kids will hit in a Sheet-backed game.

title: Topic 01, Part 09 - Personal vs.  Enterprise-Level Database Systems

best.what: personal (single-user, e.g. an app's local storage) vs enterprise (concurrent, multi-app) databases

why: Decent context (a Sheet is basically a personal-scale database) but named-product comparisons (Access, SQL Server, Oracle, SQLite) are not relevant to the course. Background reading for the teacher.

title: Topic 02, Part 01 - Database Entities
why: No caption file exists for this one (nocaps) -- judged from title only. It sits right before Characteristics of Relations and Introduction to Database Keys, both of which are excellent core concept videos in this series, so it is very likely a solid, non-SQL foundational video on entities/business concepts, but this could not be verified from the audio.

title: Topic 02, Part 02 - Characteristics of Relations

best.what: what makes a table qualify as a well-formed relation: one value per cell, unique column names, no duplicate rows

why: Directly teaches the rules for a clean Sheet tab (one value per cell, unique row, consistent columns) without ever mentioning SQL.

title: Topic 02, Part 03 - Introduction to Database Keys

best.what: unique vs non-unique keys, and why a name alone can't identify a row

why: Clear, example-driven explanation of why every Sheet tab needs an ID column.

title: Topic 02, Part 04 - Composite Keys

best.what: flight-number + date example builds intuition for keys made of two columns together

why: One of the best-taught concepts in the whole course -- the airline flight example makes composite keys immediately intuitive.

title: Topic 02, Part 05 - Candidate Keys

best.what: weighing license plate / driver's license / email / campus ID as candidates for a primary key

why: Teaches the actual design judgment of picking a good unique ID column -- a decision kids will genuinely have to make for their Sheet tabs.

title: Topic 02, Part 06 - Primary Keys and Surrogate Keys

best.what: concept of a surrogate key -- an invented ID with no real-world meaning

why: The surrogate-key concept (first 2 min) is core-quality, but roughly 6 of its 9.5 minutes are a click-through demo of setting primary keys in SQL Server Management Studio, which the kids will never use.

title: Topic 02, Part 07 - Foreign Keys and Relationships Between Tables
why: No caption file (nocaps) -- judged from title only. Foreign keys are the single most important concept for a multi-tab Sheet database, and this series has been excellent and non-SQL on concept videos so far, so this is likely strong core material, but it could not be confirmed and it is a long video (28 min) that may include a SQL Server demo like its neighbors.

title: Topic 02, Part 08 - Null Values

best.what: what null means and why it's different from 0 or an empty string
null as a business decision: does every employee have to have a department yet?

why: Great, mostly non-SQL explanation of empty cells as a design choice, directly relevant to blank cells in a Sheet.

title: Topic 02, Part 09 - Functional Dependencies

best.what: functional dependency defined via a cookie-price example

why: Correct and short, but abstract and jargon-heavy ('determinant', 'functionally dependent') -- useful groundwork for the normalization video, not standalone kid material.

title: Topic 02, Part 10 - Normalization and Normal Forms

best.what: the plain-language version: one table should hold info about only one business concept
breaking a messy sales table into order/product/customer tables

why: The core heuristic ('does this table hold more than one thing? if so, split it') is exactly the design move kids need for their Sheet; the formal 1NF/2NF/3NF/dependency machinery around it needs a guide to translate for teens.

title: Topic 03, Part 01 - Introduction to SQL

best.what: SQL is small and pattern-based, not a full programming language, and splits into DDL/DML/DCL

why: Good teaching philosophy (learn patterns, not memorization) but the payoff -- SQL is a portable standard -- doesn't matter when Gemini writes all the code. Teacher-only context for topic 3 onward.

title: Topic 03, Part 02 - Introduction to the SQL CREATE TABLE Statement
why: Pure SQL syntax and data-type selection (varchar vs char vs int/byte/bigint) plus a long SQL Server Management Studio demo -- not applicable when Gemini + Sheets is the stack.

title: Topic 03, Part 03 - Creating Primary Keys and Foreign Keys using SQL
why: Long (35 min), entirely SQL CONSTRAINT syntax and cascading update/delete behavior in SQL Server -- the underlying idea (deleting a project should clean up its team assignments) is sound but is taught here purely as SQL, not transferable to Sheets/Apps Script.

title: Topic 03, Part 04 - The SQL ALTER Statement
why: SQL syntax for altering table structure. No transferable concept beyond 'you can add a column later', which any Sheet user already knows intuitively.

title: Topic 03, Part 05 - Introduction to the Data Manipulation Language (DML)

best.what: the CRUD acronym: create/read/update/delete as the four things any app does to data

why: Short, almost SQL-free, and teaches CRUD -- a genuinely essential vocabulary word for any app the kids build, Sheets-backed or not.

title: Topic 03, Part 06 - Adding Data using the SQL INSERT INTO Statement
why: Pure INSERT INTO syntax and live SSMS demo.

title: Topic 03, Part 07 - Modifying Data using the SQL UPDATE Statement
why: SQL UPDATE syntax. The one transferable warning -- 'a missing WHERE clause changes every row, the shortest statements do the most damage' -- is a nice caution about bulk edits but too thin to justify a place on its own.

title: Topic 03, Part 08 - Deleting Data using the SQL DELETE FROM Statement
why: Pure DELETE FROM syntax.

title: Topic 03, Part 09 - Deleting Database Objects and Constraints with the SQL DROP Statement
why: SQL DROP syntax, distinguishing 'delete data' from 'delete the table itself'. Not relevant to Sheets.

title: Topic 03, Part 10 - Using SQL CHECK Constraints

best.what: check constraints validate that start date < end date before a row is allowed in

why: The concept of validating input before it's saved (start<end, hire date within company history) maps onto Sheet data-validation rules, but it's taught purely as SQL syntax here -- teacher background only.

title: Topic 03, Part 11 - Introduction to SQL SELECT Queries

best.what: SELECT as 'asking the database a question' and the result as an answer table

why: The framing (queries = questions, results = a table you can reuse) is worth keeping for a guide, but the video itself is 24 minutes of SELECT/WHERE/DISTINCT syntax and comparison operators in SQL Server -- skip for direct kid viewing.

title: Topic 03, Part 12 - Using AND and OR to Create Compound Conditions in SQL
why: SQL AND/OR/parentheses syntax with Venn-diagram support -- correct and clear but pure SQL, and Boolean AND/OR is better taught in the kids' actual scripting context (Apps Script/JS) than via SQL WHERE clauses.

title: Topic 03, Part 13 - Using IN, NOT, and BETWEEN in SQL Queries
why: SQL IN/NOT/BETWEEN syntax shortcuts.

title: Topic 03, Part 14 - Searching Based on Partial Values using the SQL LIKE Statement
why: SQL wildcard search syntax (% and _). The autocomplete tie-in is a nice real-world hook but too thin on its own; Sheets has its own search/filter functions.

title: Topic 03, Part 15 - Sorting Data in SQL using ORDER BY
why: SQL ORDER BY syntax. Sorting itself is trivial and already familiar to kids from spreadsheets.

title: Topic 03, Part 16 - Using Numeric Functions in SQL - COUNT, MIN, MAX, SUM, AVG, and STDEV

best.what: integer division vs decimal division traps when averaging whole-number columns

why: COUNT/MIN/MAX/SUM/AVG are the same names as Sheets formulas, so the concept transfers directly even though the syntax doesn't -- worth a teacher's note, not a kid watch.

title: Topic 03, Part 17 - Using the SQL GROUP BY and HAVING Statements

best.what: GROUP BY produces subtotals per category (e.g. employees per department)

why: GROUP BY/HAVING map conceptually onto pivot tables and QUERY() grouping in Sheets, which a teacher could use as an analogy, but the video itself is SQL Server syntax throughout.

title: Topic 03, Part 18 - Using Subqueries in SQL
why: No caption file (nocaps) -- judged from title only. Subqueries are an advanced SQL technique (a query nested inside another query); given every other Topic 03 video is pure SQL Server syntax, this one almost certainly is too, and it's one of the more advanced topics in the series.

title: Topic 03, Part 19 - An Overview of Joins and How to use INNER JOINS in SQL

best.what: why joins exist: each table holds one concept, joins merge them back for a real answer, with a Venn-diagram taxonomy of join types

why: The opening concept (tables are split apart, so you need a way to merge them back using matching IDs -- exactly what VLOOKUP/QUERY does across Sheet tabs) is genuinely valuable; the remaining 10 minutes are SQL JOIN...ON syntax in SQL Server.

title: Topic 03, Part 20 - Using OUTER JOINS in SQL

best.what: left/right/full outer join concept: keep unmatched rows instead of dropping them

why: The concept -- 'what happens to rows with no match, do you drop them or keep them with blanks' -- is a real design question for cross-tab Sheet lookups, but taught entirely through SQL Server syntax and demo. Teacher background only.

title: Topic 03, Part 21 - Creating and using SQL Views
why: SQL CREATE VIEW syntax and enterprise security use cases (restricting which columns/rows an employee can see) -- not relevant to a 10-15 kid classroom project.
